summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Greenfield Health through the Model Catalog: selecting open models, reading benchmark profiles, and compatibility matrices for hosted vs dedicated/private deployments. Customer focused on latency vs cost tradeoffs, quantization/precision options, and security (SOC2/KMS/VPC). Agreed next steps: share pricing/compat matrix, security pack, and schedule POC scoping plus latency benchmarks on their prompts.
topics: Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, Liam on the SE side, Jordan as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Sarah Jones: Good, thanks. Ready to see the model catalog. We want to better understand open models and how you benchmark them.
[00:12] Mike Alvarez: Yeah hi, we have some latency targets (sub-150ms for small replies) and some long prompt workloads ~2k tokens for clinical summarization.
[00:20] Priya Singh: And I want to confirm security posture: SOC2, KMS options, VPC networking - those are must-haves.
[00:28] Liam Chen: Totally understood. Quick agenda: model catalog walkthrough, how to read perf/benchmark profiles, compatibility matrix for quantization and runtime, and a short Q&A.
[00:36] Jordan Ruiz: I'll show live examples in the console and a quick SDK snippet for model selection routing.
[00:44] Maya Patel: Alright opening the model catalog... you can filter by task, model family, and performance profile. For open models we curate variants at multiple precisions - FP16, int8/4 quantized builds - and include a benchmark summary.
[00:59] Sarah Jones: When you say benchmark summary, is that latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens?
[01:04] Liam Chen: Yes, we publish p50/p95, tokens/sec, and a cost estimate normalized to our pricing unit. Note that cost is approximate - depends on batch size, KV cache hit rate, and sequence length.
[01:16] Mike Alvarez: How accurate are those numbers on our workloads? Our clinical prompts have lots of structured sections and long context.
[01:23] Liam Chen: Great question. The catalog includes the test prompt set used (you'll see examples) and a compatibility note like "long-context optimized" or "KV-cache friendly". For your 2k token workloads we recommend models labeled with "long-context" and we include quantization recommendations.
[01:36] Priya Singh: Quick security question - for dedicated or private, is key management customer controlled?
[01:41] Jordan Ruiz: Yes, Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations, and Dedicated can be configured to use customer KMS as well. For Hosted we offer managed KMS by default and a bring-your-own-key path for enterprise.
[01:51] Sarah Jones: Can you show a compatibility matrix for say, Llama-3 variants and MPT open models?
[01:58] Jordan Ruiz: Sure - here's the matrix. (screen share) Left column model family, columns are runtime features: FP16, int8-4, KV cache support, sequence length tested, recommended hardware (A100, H100, T4-ish), and any special kernels required.
[02:12] Maya Patel: For example Llama-3-8B has an int8-4 quantized build that runs well on A100 and H100 with our optimized kernels; for T4 or older cards we recommend lower sequence lengths or the FP16 variant.
[02:25] Mike Alvarez: Whoops - are those numbers tested on your dedicated clusters or emulated?
[02:30] Liam Chen: Benchmarks are run on our representative hardware pools - dedicated A100/H100 clusters in our lab - and we also publish hosted latency profiles which include multi-tenant variance. For strict SLA work we recommend reserved dedicated runs.
[02:43] Sarah Jones: Ok and can we run an apples-to-apples test against our on-prem hardware?
[02:47] Liam Chen: Absolutely - as part of POC scoping we can provide benchmark scripts and sample prompt sets so you can run locally or we can run them in our lab. We've found some transcription diffs in kernel availability between driver versions, so we include exact driver + CUDA + cuDNN env details in the repo.
[03:02] Priya Singh: About data residency - if we host in your dedicated region, do logs leave our VPC?
[03:08] Jordan Ruiz: For Private deployments logs are customer-controlled. For Dedicated we offer options: we can retain logs within a customer-managed VPC peering or stream minimal telemetry for SLOs; full audit logs can be retained per contract.
[03:20] Maya Patel: Now switching to the Console live: here's how you pick a model for text-generation API. We show the catalog card with tags - latency profile, quality score from our evals, cost estimate, and compatibility notes.
[03:35] (screen: model card Llama-3-8B-int8-4 displayed)
[03:38] Mike Alvarez: That "quality score" - how do you compute it?
[03:41] Liam Chen: It's a composite from our eval harness: pass@k-like metrics on curated prompt sets, hallucination rate, and downstream task quality (for summarization/QA). It's meant to help compare models on a workload family, not absolute truth.
[03:54] Sarah Jones: Any note on instruction-following fine-tuning? We have internal prompts and want lower hallucination.
[03:59] Jordan Ruiz: We annotate whether a model is instruction-tuned and supply recommended prompt templates. For customers doing instruction-tuning we support hosted fine-tuning paths for some partners and private fine-tune tooling in the Private bundle.
[04:12] Maya Patel: On the API side you can pin model versions and set rollout policies - e.g., traffic split 90/10 between a quantized candidate and baseline, automatic fallback to FP16 if quality drops.
[04:22] Mike Alvarez: That autoswitching - does it evaluate quality on the fly?
[04:25] Liam Chen: We can tie rollouts to quality monitors that use prompt set checks and regex-based safety filters; if a regression triggers we automatically shift traffic to the fallback.
[04:34] (timestamp jump)
[04:50] Sarah Jones: Can you talk about batching and how to tune for low latency vs throughput?
[04:55] Liam Chen: Sure: our runtime supports continuous batching with latency SLOs. You set a max batching window and max batch size. For sub-150ms interactive cases you keep small batch windows and prefer dedicated hardware; for high throughput background tasks you increase batch windows and gain cost savings per token.
[05:12] Mike Alvarez: Do you have recommendations for our mixed workload - short queries for triage UI and long summaries?
[05:18] Jordan Ruiz: We usually route short interactive traffic to a low-latency pool (smaller model/FP16), and long summarization to a long-context-optimized model in a different queue, or run it on dedicated capacity with larger batch sizes. Smart routing can be policy-driven in the Console.
[05:32] Priya Singh: On encryption at rest: do you encrypt model caches/KV store?
[05:36] Liam Chen: Yes, KV cache and disk swap are encrypted; in Private you control the KMS; in Dedicated we can use customer KMS.
[05:43] Sarah Jones: How are models validated for PII leakage?
[05:46] Maya Patel: We run privacy/regression evals as part of onboarding - prompt-based checks, and we can run your proprietary prompt set through a sandbox to assess PII propensity.
[05:55] Mike Alvarez: About the model catalog filters - can we add custom tags or internal quality markers?
[05:59] Jordan Ruiz: You can add workspace-level tags and pin models for routes. In Private you can add internal model labels and store custom eval results in the Console.
[06:07] (background cross talk, small interruption)
[06:12] Sarah Jones: Let's discuss pricing briefly - is pricing per-token the same for quantized models?
[06:17] Maya Patel: Pricing is per-token compute unit but we often give adjusted rates for quantized variants because they run at higher throughput; the catalog shows normalized cost per 1k tokens that factors in throughput gains.
[06:28] Mike Alvarez: For long jobs with 2k tokens - how does cost per token change?
[06:31] Liam Chen: You usually see slightly higher per-token cost for long contexts because attention scales quadratically, but KV cache reuse and chunking strategies reduce effective cost for repeated contexts. We show cost curves in the benchmark sheets.
[06:45] Sarah Jones: Can you email that benchmark sheet and the compatibility matrix?
[06:48] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll attach the sheet.
[06:50] (15 minute demo sped through model cards and console features; timestamps continue sporadically)
[21:10] Mike Alvarez: On the SDK snippet, how do you call a specific quantized model and set routing to dedicated?
[21:15] Jordan Ruiz: Example: client.responses.create({ model: "llama-3-8b-int8-4", route: "dedicated-eu-west-2", max_tokens: 512, timeout_ms: 2000 }) - and you can set per-route autoscaling and burst windows in the Console.
[21:30] Priya Singh: For audit logs, are token-level request logs retained? We need to ensure we can redact PHI and configure retention windows.
[21:38] Liam Chen: We support redaction rules and retention windows; token-level logs can be disabled and aggregated metrics provided instead. For PHI we advise Private with customer-managed audit logging to meet HIPAA controls.
[21:52] Sarah Jones: Are there references or public benchmarks we can look at?
[21:56] Maya Patel: We have public benchmark docs and an eval repo - will share link. Also we can run a small Redwood-hosted benchmark using your prompt set and share results next week.
[22:10] Mike Alvarez: That would be helpful. Also curious about inference kernels - you mentioned specialized kernels; do we need specific drivers?
[22:16] Liam Chen: Certain kernels require newer CUDA/drivers; we include exact driver and kernel versions in the catalog notes. If you're on older infra, the compatibility matrix flags unsupported optimizations.
[22:30] (tension) Sarah Jones: What are typical lead times for Dedicated provisioning?
[22:34] Maya Patel: For reserved Dedicated it's usually 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and region; Private on-prem we can do an engagement plan that ranges 4-12 weeks depending on integration.
[22:45] Priya Singh: Last security question - do you support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
[22:49] Jordan Ruiz: Yes, SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and we can map roles to routes and namespaces.
[22:56] Maya Patel: Quick recap and next steps: we'll send the model catalog pricing/compatibility matrix, SOC2/security pack, and benchmark scripts. Proposed POC scoping call next week.
[23:10] Sarah Jones: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[23:13] Mike Alvarez: Thanks, appreciate the demo.
[23:15] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[23:18] Maya Patel: Ok we'll follow up with the materials and the calendar invite.
[23:22] (call ends)
notes: Customer emphasized 2k token workload and sub-150ms interactive latency target
Security required SOC2 + KMS + VPC controls - leaning toward Dedicated/Private for PHI workloads
POC: run Redwood-hosted and dedicated benchmarks on customer's prompt set
